mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4% over the prior month reduces the discount rate applied to expected future earnings, lowering the present value of equity cash flows and thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns in the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4% in the preceding month
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during similar non-tightening periods (p > 0.05 in t-test).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which raises consumer confidence and corporate earnings expectations, pushing S&P 500 forward returns positive over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by > 10% in a month while UNRATE falls by > 0.2 percentage points
failure_condition: No significant correlation between PAYEMS acceleration and SPX 60-day forward returns (R > 0.1, p > 0.05 in Granger causality test).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly rise in personal consumption expenditures (CPIAUCSL) above 0.5% y/y for three consecutive months indicates accelerating demand growth, which anticipates stronger corporate revenue and supports positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL monthly growth rate exceeds 0.5% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05) during confirmed demand acceleration periods.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below -2% suggests weakening supply-side constraints, which reduces inventory pressures and allows for higher investment spending, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by > 2% in a month
failure_condition: During INDPRO contractions, SPX 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during baseline expansion phases (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the 1-month change in the federal funds rate turns positive (i.e., rates rise), the real discount rate increases, reducing the present value of expected equity cash flows and driving S&P 500 forward returns negative over the next 20 days in a tightening cycle.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases in the prior month
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns during tightening are not significantly worse than during stable periods (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in unemployment (UNRATE) and a sustained rise in hourly wage growth (not directly observable but proxy via labor market strength indicators such as PAYEMS) predicts stronger consumer demand and corporate profit expectations, pushing S&P 500 forward returns positive over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls by > 0.1% while PAYEMS shows upward momentum
failure_condition: No significant positive SPX 60-day returns coincide with the combined signal (Granger causality p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A regime shift to post-crisis normalization in macroeconomic variables (e.g., FEDFUNDS > 1%, UNRATE < 5%, CPIAUCSL > 2% y/y) creates a structural change that increases risk premia and produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: All three normalization thresholds are met for three consecutive months
failure_condition: During such regimes, SPX 20-day returns are not statistically lower than in pre-crisis baseline periods (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged monthly decline in retail sales (not directly observable but proxy via industrial production and consumer confidence; however, per evidence constraints we use available proxies) combined with rising inflation (CPIAUCSL) suggests supply-side disruptions and higher input costs, which depresses equity valuations and drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO declines for two consecutive months while CPIAUCSL increases by > 0.2% in the same period
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns during such episodes are not statistically worse than during stable supply conditions (p > 0.05).
